item.title: Giga Press Factory DX: From Field Signals to Virtual Commissioning
item.description:

A dedicated public source repository has not been separated for this project. The GitHub URL is a project index, not evidence that another repository contains this implementation.

Portfolio summary: Problem–Role–Action–Result–Evidence

Item Verified scope
Problem Process sequences and parameter assumptions could only be checked late with physical equipment, while PLC, SCADA, and virtual-model data integrity was hard to review in advance.
Role In a ten-person team, I worked in the Digital Twin group on AI-model selection/training, communications setup, and technical research. Ladder and SCADA implementation belonged to other team members and is not presented as my individual work.
Action I mapped the Factory I/O–PLC–SCADA–OPC UA data path, reviewed the DQN control candidate, and defined the boundary between control, monitoring, and AI-assisted optimization.
Result The team integrated process flow, Ladder/Factory I/O, SCADA, web, and AI-extension concepts into one demonstration and report. The cited 50–75% setup reduction and 50% expansion-labor reduction are expected benefits/targets, not measured factory outcomes.
Evidence The team report’s R&R table, architecture, result, and expected-benefit slides; no dedicated public source repository.

Resume bullets

  • Owned AI-model selection/training and OPC UA communications scope in a ten-person manufacturing-DX project that connected Factory I/O, PLC, SCADA, and a virtual commissioning scenario.
  • Converted battery-line FAT/SAT experience into failure-oriented checks covering missing sensors, communication delay, restart conditions, and safe PLC authority.
  • Kept the report’s 50–75% setup and 50% expansion-effort figures as pre-production targets rather than presenting them as measured plant savings.

Interview STAR

  • Situation: High-capital equipment creates late discovery risk because control logic and data integrity are difficult to test before physical trial.
  • Task: My scope was to define where AI and communications fit so that control and monitoring layers used consistent data without giving AI unrestricted equipment authority.
  • Action: I organized the OPC UA data flow, reviewed DQN as an optimization candidate, and kept deterministic control and safety checks inside the PLC boundary.
  • Result: The team produced an integrated simulation and report. Quantified values remained expected benefits until controlled before/after measurement is available.
